title: 159. Young Putin, the KGB and the Soviet Union

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余韵》。

sentences.en: And we would like to go over to Crawford, Texas, where we are joined by a special gueSt.
sentences.zh: 我们现在连线德克萨斯州的克劳福德，那里有一位特别嘉宾加入我们。

sentences.en: I'll answer the question.
sentences.zh: 我会回答这个问题。

sentences.en: I looked the man in the eye.
sentences.zh: 我直视了他的眼睛。

sentences.en: I found it to be very straightforward and trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他非常坦率、值得信赖。

sentences.en: We had a very good dialogue.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了非常好的对话。

sentences.en: I was able to get a sense of his soul.
sentences.zh: 我得以窥见了他的灵魂。

sentences.en: He's a man deeply committed to his country and the best interests of his country.
sentences.zh: 他是一个深爱自己国家、一心为国家利益着想的人。

sentences.en: And I appreciated so very much the frank dialogue.
sentences.zh: 我非常感激那次坦诚的对话。

sentences.en: There was no kind of diplomatic chit-chat, trying to throw each other off balance.
sentences.zh: 没有那种试图让对方失去平衡的外交客套话。

sentences.en: There was a straightforward dialogue.
sentences.zh: 那是一场开门见山的对话。

sentences.en: And that's the beginning of a very constructive relationship.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常有建设性的关系的开端。

sentences.en: I wouldn't have invited him to my ranch if I didn't trust him.
sentences.zh: 如果我不信任他，我就不会邀请他到我的牧场来。

sentences.en: That was my brilliant impression of George W.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是我对乔治·W·布什的精彩模仿。

sentences.en: Bush.
sentences.zh: 布什。

sentences.en: It wasn't actually.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是。

sentences.en: That really was George Bush.
sentences.zh: 那真的是乔治·布什本人。

sentences.en: That was our first presidential gueSt.
sentences.zh: 那是我们第一位总统嘉宾。

sentences.en: And that was the occasion in 2001 of his first meeting with President Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 那是在2001年他与弗拉基米尔·普京总统首次会晤时的场景。

sentences.en: In light of the current situation, we thought that it would be interesting to look at some of the historical context.
sentences.zh: 鉴于当前局势，我们认为回顾一些历史背景会很有意思。

sentences.en: We've already done an episode on the history of Ukraine, but we thought that it would be, you know, I mean, essentially everyone is asking, how did we get here?
sentences.zh: 我们已经做过一期关于乌克兰历史的节目，但我们觉得，你知道，我的意思是，基本上每个人都在问，我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: What is it that's prompted Putin to do what he's doing?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么促使普京采取了现在的行动？

sentences.en: You know, what is the background?
sentences.zh: 你知道，背景是什么？

sentences.en: What is there an explanation for it that can be discovered in history, I suppose, and in his, specifically in his biography?
sentences.zh: 我想，在历史中，特别是在他的个人传记中，是否能找到对此的解释？

sentences.en: This is a field that you are much, much more familiar with than I am.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你比我熟悉得多的领域。

sentences.en: But I guess I lived through it, so a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 但我猜我亲历了那个时代，所以了解很多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think, Tom, there's that apocryphal saying by Napoleon, isn't there, that if you know the world, if you've studied the world when a man was 20, you know how his mind works.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我想拿破仑有句托名名言，不是吗？如果你了解这个世界，如果你研究过一个人20岁时的世界，你就知道他的思维方式。

sentences.en: And Vladimir Putin, like any Russian of his generation, he's born in 1952, has lived through the most colossal, almost unimaginable political, economic,
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京像他那一代的任何俄罗斯人一样，他出生于1952年，经历了前苏联和俄罗斯最巨大、几乎难以想象的政治、经济、

sentences.en: kind of social changes in the former Soviet Union and Russia.
sentences.zh: 以及社会变革。

sentences.en: And if we, and it's only by understanding what's happened to him and his country, I think that you can actually get, get into his, into his, well,
sentences.zh: 如果我们，而且我认为只有通过了解发生在他和他国家身上的事情，你才能真正进入他的，进入他的，嗯，

sentences.en: attempt to get into his head and to understand why Russia is now as it is.
sentences.zh: 尝试进入他的内心，去理解为什么俄罗斯现在是这个样子。

sentences.en: So now it's becoming, you know, it appears to be becoming this pariah state, kind of shut off behind a new iron curtain of sanctions.
sentences.zh: 所以现在它正在变成，你知道，看起来正在变成一个被排斥的国家，被关在了一道新的制裁铁幕之后。

sentences.en: How on earth has it got here?
sentences.zh: 它到底是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: And that's what we're going to try and try and investigate.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要尝试去调查的内容。

sentences.en: I mean, Dominic, you're, of course, it's been an absolutely convulsive period of change, but there is also always the historian's question, change or continuity.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我的意思是，当然，这是一个极其动荡的变革时期，但历史学家总会问一个问题：是变革还是延续？

sentences.en: And you could say, I mean, people have been saying that actually not that much has changed.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，人们一直在说其实并没有发生太大的变化。

sentences.en: That the Soviet Union was a political system founded on lies, founded on a profound suspicion of the outside, founded on an emphasis on military prowess over everything else.
sentences.zh: 苏联是一个建立在谎言之上的政治体制，建立在对外部世界的深刻怀疑之上，建立在将军事实力置于一切之上的强调之上。

sentences.en: And you could say that Russia today is showing, you know, much the same.
sentences.zh: 你可以说今天的俄罗斯表现出来的，你知道，也是大同小异。

sentences.en: Is the air of that.
sentences.zh: 是那种氛围。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't, normally I'm a great determinist in this podcast, but I don't think that's really true, actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不，通常在这个播客里我是一个坚定的决定论者，但我觉得那其实并不完全正确。

sentences.en: I think that misses, you know, obviously Putin himself is a product of the Soviet system, which we'll go into in a second.
sentences.zh: 我认为这忽略了，你知道，显然普京本人就是苏联体制的产物，我们稍后会深入探讨。

sentences.en: But I think when you actually go through the period of change, you see that there were alternative paths that Russia could have taken.
sentences.zh: 但我认为当你真正回顾那个变革时期时，你会发现俄罗斯本可以有其他的选择。

sentences.en: And Russia isn't fated to be this sort of violent, you know, nationalistic kind of hellhole that so many people imagine.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯并非注定要成为许多人想象中的那种暴力、民族主义的“地狱”。

sentences.en: You know, what happened in the USSR in the 1980s and then in Russia in the 1990s, there are all kinds of contingencies and twists and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，20世纪80年代的苏联和90年代的俄罗斯发生的事情，充满了各种偶然性和曲折等等。

sentences.en: And there were alternative futures for Russia, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将要看到的，俄罗斯本有其他的未来。

sentences.en: But just before we go to look at the last decade of the Soviet Union, you talked about the idea that Russia wasn't fated to become what it is now.
sentences.zh: 但在我们回顾苏联的最后十年之前，你谈到了俄罗斯并非注定要变成现在这个样子的观点。

sentences.en: But that idea of fate, the idea that Russia has a particular destiny, I mean, that is something that is very strong in Russian culture and actually much older, of course,
sentences.zh: 但那种宿命论，即俄罗斯有着某种特殊命运的观念，我的意思是，这在俄罗斯文化中非常强烈，而且当然比共产主义要古老得多。

sentences.en: than communism.
sentences.zh: 比共产主义更古老。

sentences.en: Yeah, the sort of Dostoevsky and Tolstoy, and there are two different things on there, Dostoevsky and Tolstoy.
sentences.zh: 是的，陀思妥耶夫斯基和托尔斯泰，这里有两件不同的事情，陀思妥耶夫斯基和托尔斯泰。

sentences.en: But the sort of the idea of Russia having this almost, as you would say, Tom, this almost kind of sacral destiny, you know, the third Rome, the home of orthodoxy,
sentences.zh: 但那种认为俄罗斯拥有，正如你所说的，汤姆，这种近乎神圣命运的观念，你知道，第三罗马，东正教的家园，

sentences.en: kind of on the edge of Europe, half in Europe, half out.
sentences.zh: 处于欧洲边缘，一半在欧洲，一半在欧洲之外。

sentences.en: But, I mean, that is very deeply rooted in Russia's sense of itself, the sense of embattlement, a sense of distrust of the outside, but also a fascination with it.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，这在俄罗斯的自我认知中根深蒂固，那种被围困感，对外部的不信任感，但同时也对外部充满着迷。

sentences.en: So, yes, all those things are there.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，所有这些因素都存在。

sentences.en: But there is a sort of slightly stereotypical way we talk about Russia.
sentences.zh: 但我们谈论俄罗斯的方式有一种略显刻板的印象。

sentences.en: So we always talk about, I mean, even George Bush did it there when he talked about knowing Putin's soul.
sentences.zh: 所以我们总是谈论，我的意思是，连乔治·布什在谈到了解普京的灵魂时也是这样。

sentences.en: The idea of the Russians having a soul that you must understand that is incredibly deep and dark.
sentences.zh: 认为俄罗斯人拥有一个你必须去理解的、极其深邃而黑暗的灵魂。

sentences.en: I mean, nobody says that about, you know...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没人会那样说，你知道……

sentences.en: Belgium.
sentences.zh: 比利时。

sentences.en: Yeah, Belgium.
sentences.zh: 是的，比利时。

sentences.en: No, nobody says that about Belgium.
sentences.zh: 不，没人会那样说比利时。

sentences.en: Maybe Bart Van Leeu, our previous guest, would say that.
sentences.zh: 也许我们之前的嘉宾巴特·范·勒乌会这么说。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, today, when you apply the word exceptionalism to countries, it's generally a pejorative.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我的意思是，今天当你把“例外论”这个词用在国家身上时，它通常是一个贬义词。

sentences.en: So people are very sniffy about the idea that there might be British exceptionalism or French exceptionalism.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对可能存在“英国例外论”或“法国例外论”的想法非常不屑。

sentences.en: Or American exceptionalism.
sentences.zh: 或者“美国例外论”。

sentences.en: Even though, clearly, you know, I mean, they are all very exceptional countries.
sentences.zh: 尽管很明显，你知道，我的意思是，它们都是非常例外的国家。

sentences.en: But in Russia, it seems to be something that is pretty fundamental to the way that not just Russian politicians, but large numbers of people within the country think of Russia.
sentences.zh: 但在俄罗斯，这似乎是不仅俄罗斯政客，而且国内大量民众思考俄罗斯方式的根本所在。

sentences.en: Would you say that's fair or am I stereotyping that?
sentences.zh: 你会说这公平吗，还是我在刻板印象化？

sentences.en: I think it absolutely...
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对……

sentences.en: No, I think it probably is fair.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这大概是公平的。

sentences.en: I think that's the way that a lot of Russians are told to think about themselves, that they have an exceptional, a unique past and a kind of exceptional destiny.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是许多俄罗斯人被灌输的看待自己的方式，即他们拥有一个例外的、独特的过去和一种例外的命运。

sentences.en: And we do think of Russia typically as having an exceptional character.
sentences.zh: 我们确实通常认为俄罗斯具有一种例外的性格。

sentences.en: Outsiders do.
sentences.zh: 局外人是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And that's all that stuff about the Russian soul and about, you know, Russians are terribly kind of warm people, but they're also...
sentences.zh: 这就是所有关于俄罗斯灵魂的东西，关于，你知道，俄罗斯人是非常热情的人，但他们也……

sentences.en: The price of human life is lower and all that sort of thing that you hear so often.
sentences.zh: 人命的价格更低，诸如此类你经常听到的事情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think there is a kind of exceptionalism, both projected from the outside, but also believed inside.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为确实存在一种例外论，既是从外部投射出来的，也是内部所信仰的。

sentences.en: I mean, it was expressed very unsettlingly by Putin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，普京对此的表达非常令人不安。

sentences.en: And I may be paraphrasing him here, and I, you know, this may be disinformation, but didn't he say something to the effect, talking with regard to nuclear weapons,
sentences.zh: 我可能是在转述他的话，而且，你知道，这可能是虚假信息，但他不是在谈论核武器时说了类似的话吗，

sentences.en: that a world without Russia wouldn't be a world...
sentences.zh: 说一个没有俄罗斯的世界，那就不叫世界了……

sentences.en: You know, why should the world exist if it exists without Russia?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果世界没有了俄罗斯，那它为什么还要存在呢？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And not only has he said that, by the way, but his kind of mouthpieces on Russian state television have used exactly the same line.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，不仅他这么说过，他在俄罗斯国家电视台的那些喉舌也用了完全相同的台词。

sentences.en: So that's, yeah, a well-worn line, actually, in the sort of Putinist ideology.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这在普京主义的意识形态中确实是一句老生常谈的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay, so a bit unsettling, coming from people with the largest quantity of nuclear weapons on the face of the planet.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于那些拥有地球上最大规模核武器的人来说，这确实有点令人不安。

sentences.en: But something that, as we said, can be traced back to the Tsarist period, but obviously gets a particular refinement under communism,
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所说，这可以追溯到沙皇时期，但在共产主义统治下显然得到了某种特定的提炼，

sentences.en: where what had been the Russian Empire becomes the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 那时曾经的俄罗斯帝国变成了苏联。

sentences.en: And as the Soviet Union is one of two superpowers and sees itself charged with a historical destiny, it is the midwife of world communism.
sentences.zh: 作为两个超级大国之一，苏联认为自己肩负着历史使命，它是世界共产主义的助产士。

sentences.en: That has sustained it throughout decades of transformation and upheaval.
sentences.zh: 这支撑了它几十年的转型和动荡。

sentences.en: By the 70s, when Putin is coming of age, that sense of purpose and of destiny perhaps is starting to fade.
sentences.zh: 到了70年代，当普京步入成年时，那种目标感和使命感或许开始消退了。

sentences.en: It's the age of Brezhnev, a man with kind of insanely huge eyebrows and a kind of rigor mortis starts, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是勃列日涅夫时代，一个有着极其浓密眉毛和一种僵尸般状态的人，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, they're all kind of basically dead.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们基本上都快死了。

sentences.en: They are constantly getting colds, but keep them in their beds for five years.
sentences.zh: 他们总是感冒，但却在床上躺了五年。

sentences.en: They wear nothing but overcoats.
sentences.zh: 他们只穿大衣。

sentences.en: They wear things under the overcoats, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他们在大衣里面还穿了东西。

sentences.en: Do they?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: I've never seen any evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过任何证据。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你是对的。

sentences.en: It's always snowing.
sentences.zh: 总是下着雪。

sentences.en: So what's going on?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: So Putin is born in Leningrad, St. Petersburg in 1952, and he's from a working class family.
sentences.zh: 普京1952年出生于列宁格勒（圣彼得堡），来自一个工人阶级家庭。

sentences.en: His parents work in a factory and he goes to Leningrad State University in 1970, I think, and he's there for five years.
sentences.zh: 他的父母在工厂工作，我想他在1970年进入列宁格勒国立大学，在那里待了五年。

sentences.en: And so he comes of age in the Brezhnev era, as you say, and it's an age of it is not an age of revolutionary zeal at all.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，他在勃列日涅夫时代成年，那根本不是一个充满革命热情的时代。

sentences.en: So you mentioned communism and a sort of sense of communist zeal, but that really isn't what typifies the Brezhnev regime.
sentences.zh: 你提到了共产主义和某种共产主义热情，但这确实不是勃列日涅夫政权的典型特征。

sentences.en: The Brezhnev regime is all about stability, and there's a kind of ordinariness to it.
sentences.zh: 勃列日涅夫政权的核心是稳定，而且有一种平凡感。

sentences.en: So for most people who are alive in the Soviet Union at that point, the Soviet Union is all they've ever known.
sentences.zh: 所以对于当时生活在苏联的大多数人来说，苏联就是他们所知的一切。

sentences.en: And everybody in the world, in America, in Britain, in Western Europe, and in the Soviet Union, thinks the Soviet Union is going to probably be around forever.
sentences.zh: 世界上每个人，在美国、英国、西欧和苏联，都认为苏联可能会永远存在下去。

sentences.en: It is, as you say, one of the two superpowers.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它是两个超级大国之一。

sentences.en: It's sclerotic.
sentences.zh: 它已经硬化了。

sentences.en: The economy is producing enough to keep people happy, so they're fed.
sentences.zh: 经济生产足以让人们感到满足，所以他们有饭吃。

sentences.en: They've actually got more consumer goods than ever before.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上拥有的消费品比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: You know, Robert Service in his History of Russia says, I think he uses the phrase, most Russian workers had never had it so good as they had it in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，罗伯特·瑟维斯在《俄罗斯史》中说，我想他用了这样的短语：大多数俄罗斯工人在20世纪70年代的生活是前所未有的好。

sentences.en: So they've got fridges, they go on holiday there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有冰箱，他们去度假。

sentences.en: You know, life's okay.
sentences.zh: 你知道，生活还过得去。

sentences.en: But relatively, relatively, they've never had it.
sentences.zh: 但相对而言，相对而言，他们从未有过。

sentences.en: I mean, they've never had it so good, but relative to the capitalist WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的生活从未如此美好，但相对于资本主义的西方而言。

sentences.en: Of course, it's falling further.
sentences.zh: 当然，它在进一步落后。

sentences.en: Economically, they're starting to fall behind.
sentences.zh: 在经济上，他们开始落后了。

sentences.en: And the prosperity, the apparent prosperity of the 70s is based on a fiction.
sentences.zh: 而70年代那种表面的繁荣是建立在虚构之上的。

sentences.en: So it's based on a sclerotic, incredibly complicated, top-down sort of system, you know, the sort of parodies of sort of state planning and tractor statistics and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以它是建立在一个僵化、极其复杂、自上而下的体系之上，你知道，那种国家计划、拖拉机统计数据之类的讽刺，

sentences.en: They're all rooted in truth.
sentences.zh: 它们都植根于事实。

sentences.en: But it's also rooted in high oil prices.
sentences.zh: 但它也植根于高油价。

sentences.en: So high world, they're almost living a bit of an illusion.
sentences.zh: 所以世界油价高，他们几乎生活在一种幻觉中。

sentences.en: Because when the oil price falls in the 1980s, that's going to pull the rug out from the system.
sentences.zh: 因为当80年代油价下跌时，那将抽走这个体系的基石。

sentences.en: And Brezhnev, as you say, I mean, he's not Stalin.
sentences.zh: 而且勃列日涅夫，正如你所说，我的意思是，他不是斯大林。

sentences.en: You know, he's nothing like Stalin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他一点也不像斯大林。

sentences.en: He's not.
sentences.zh: 他不是。

sentences.en: It's still a very autocratic system.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个非常专制的体系。

sentences.en: It's one that represses dissidents and shoves them into psychiatric hospitals.
sentences.zh: 它镇压异见人士并将他们关进精神病院。

sentences.en: But it doesn't kill lots of people.
sentences.zh: 但它不会杀很多人。

sentences.en: So life kind of, you know, goes on.
sentences.zh: 所以生活就那样，你知道，继续着。

sentences.en: And for a young man like Putin, his ambition is to join the KGB.
sentences.zh: 对于像普京这样的年轻人来说，他的抱负是加入克格勃。

sentences.en: Supposedly, he applies to join and they say to him, you don't apply.
sentences.zh: 据说他申请加入，他们对他说，你不能申请。

sentences.en: You know, we contact you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，是我们联系你。

sentences.en: But they kind of make a note of him because they know that he's loyal and hardworking and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实留意了他，因为他们知道他忠诚、勤奋，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So for him, he thinks he's joining the intelligence service of actually the world's great power.
sentences.zh: 所以对他来说，他认为自己加入的是世界大国的间谍机构。

sentences.en: Because the 1970s is a terrible decade for the kind of the United States.
sentences.zh: 因为70年代对美国来说是一个糟糕的十年。

sentences.en: It's the decade of Nixon and Carter and Vietnam and this sort of introspection.
sentences.zh: 那是尼克松、卡特、越南战争和这种内省的十年。

sentences.en: And the Soviet Union, there's a sort of sense that the Soviet Union might even be winning the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 而在苏联，有一种苏联甚至可能正在赢得冷战的感觉。

sentences.en: Burying them.
sentences.zh: 埋葬他们。

sentences.en: Burying them, yes, as Khrushchev said to Nixon.
sentences.zh: 是的，埋葬他们，正如赫鲁晓夫对尼克松所说的那样。

sentences.en: So there's this sort of false image, I think, that people have about their own society in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为人们对70年代自己社会的看法有一种错误的形象。

sentences.en: And there are some people at the top of the Soviet regime.
sentences.zh: 在苏联政权高层有一些人。

sentences.en: So in particular, the man who's going to succeed, Burying them, who's a man called Yuri Andropov, who is the head of the KGB.
sentences.zh: 特别是那个即将继任的人，埋葬他们，那个叫尤里·安德罗波夫的人，他是克格勃的负责人。

sentences.en: There are some people who know that there are deep problems, that Russia has, you know, I say Russia.
sentences.zh: 有些人知道存在严重的问题，俄罗斯有，你知道，我说的是俄罗斯。

sentences.en: The Soviet Union has huge problems with alcoholism, with absenteeism, that its birth rate is struggling.
sentences.zh: 苏联在酗酒、旷工方面有巨大的问题，出生率也在挣扎。

sentences.en: That, you know, high rates of corruption, all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，高腐败率，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: But Putin doesn't see this as a young man, I wouldn't have said.
sentences.zh: 但我不会说普京作为一个年轻人能看到这一点。

sentences.en: Well, two questions.
sentences.zh: 好吧，两个问题。

sentences.en: First of all, Putin, is he a committed communist as a young man?
sentences.zh: 首先，普京年轻时是一个坚定的共产主义者吗？

sentences.en: Or is he a committed nationalist?
sentences.zh: 还是说他是一个坚定的民族主义者？

sentences.en: What's the balance there?
sentences.zh: 这两者之间是如何平衡的？

sentences.en: If you read sort of his semi-official biography, it says that he reads, you know, he enjoys reading Marxist, Leninist books when he's at school.
sentences.zh: 如果你读过他那本半官方的传记，上面说他在学校时喜欢读马克思和列宁的著作。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's a bit like Christianity, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这有点像基督教，汤姆。

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: It is, in this sense.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说是的。

sentences.en: There's a difference between being a Christian in the second century AD and being a Christian in the 16th century when everybody's a Christian.
sentences.zh: 公元二世纪的基督徒和十六世纪人人都是基督徒时的基督徒，这两者是有区别的。

sentences.en: And, you know, you're not a radical, you're not a rebel, you're not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你并不是一个激进分子，不是一个叛逆者，不一定非得是。

sentences.en: Well, you might be in the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在十六世纪你可能就是了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but you might be a good Christian, but none of those things.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但你可能是一个虔诚的基督徒，却完全不是那些激进或叛逆的人。

sentences.en: You might just be an apparatchik.
sentences.zh: 你可能只是个官僚机器里的一颗螺丝钉。

sentences.en: And I think he's a communist in the sense that he's listened to everything he's been told and that provides his framework.
sentences.zh: 我认为他之所以是共产主义者，是因为他听从了所有被灌输的东西，而这构成了他的思想框架。

sentences.en: But I don't think he burns with the zeal of social justice or with revolutionary enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 但我并不认为他内心燃烧着社会正义的狂热或革命的热情。

sentences.en: Actually, Tom, I think a lot of the people who are running the show don't burn with revolutionary zeal.
sentences.zh: 事实上，汤姆，我觉得很多当权者内心并没有燃烧着革命的狂热。

sentences.en: OK, that was my other question.
sentences.zh: 好的，那是我另一个问题。

sentences.en: But I think before I ask that, let's take a quick break.
sentences.zh: 但在我问那个问题之前，让我们先休息一下。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: So we're about 15 minutes in and to be fair, we have barely scratched the surface.
sentences.zh: 现在节目进行了大约15分钟，平心而论，我们才刚刚触及皮毛。

sentences.en: So what we're thinking of doing this week is having a slightly different release schedule from usual.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这周打算采用一种与往常略有不同的发布时间表。

sentences.en: We're going to release these episodes charting the fall of the Soviet Union, the chaos in Russia in the 1990s and the rise of Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 我们将发布这些记录苏联解体、九十年代俄罗斯混乱以及弗拉基米尔·普京崛起的剧集。

sentences.en: Well, we're going to release these over the next three days.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们将在接下来的三天内发布这些内容。

sentences.en: So we're going to break them into slightly more digestible and accessible chunks because it's such a complicated and an important subject.
sentences.zh: 我们将把它们拆分成更易于消化和理解的片段，因为这是一个非常复杂且重要的主题。

sentences.en: Now, we will obviously return to our usual schedule next week.
sentences.zh: 当然，下周我们会恢复正常的发布时间表。

sentences.en: But we had such a big response to our Russia and Ukraine episode and so many requests for us to do these stories as well.
sentences.zh: 但我们关于俄罗斯和乌克兰的那期节目反响巨大，很多人要求我们讲述这些故事。

sentences.en: We hope you understand.
sentences.zh: 希望你们能理解。

sentences.en: And I have to say, if you cannot wait for the rest of the story, if you literally cannot wait till tomorrow morning, then why would you be able to wait?
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，如果你等不及想听剩下的故事，如果你真的等不到明天早上，那么你又怎么可能等得下去呢？

sentences.en: Tom, there's another option for people, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，大家还有另一个选择，对吧？

sentences.en: There is indeed, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yes, you can join the Rest is History Club.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以加入《历史的余味》俱乐部。

sentences.en: And we appreciate that we've gained a lot of new listeners over the last couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 我们很感谢过去几周里新增了许多听众。

sentences.en: So let's just quickly explain how it works.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们快速解释一下它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So the Rest is History Club members get certain benefits like, as Dominic just said, early access to new episodes.
sentences.zh: 《历史的余味》俱乐部成员可以获得一些福利，正如多米尼克刚才所说，可以提前收听新剧集。

sentences.en: You get ad-free listening.
sentences.zh: 你可以享受无广告收听。

sentences.en: You get a bonus episode each week where Dominic and I review your messages, review the episodes that we've done, feedback to that, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 每周你还能获得一期额外剧集，我和多米尼克会在里面回复你们的留言，回顾我们做过的节目，反馈意见，诸如此类。

sentences.en: We do live shows on YouTube once a month.
sentences.zh: 我们每月会在YouTube上进行一次直播。

sentences.en: So what have we done, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 我们都做过些什么，多米尼克？

sentences.en: We've done the 60s, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我们做过六十年代，对吧？

sentences.en: We've done assassinations.
sentences.zh: 我们做过暗杀事件。

sentences.en: We did clubs.
sentences.zh: 我们做过俱乐部。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Great clubs of history.
sentences.zh: 历史上伟大的俱乐部。

sentences.en: All kinds of stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的内容。

sentences.en: So stuff that you wouldn't otherwise get to hear.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是你平时听不到的内容。

sentences.en: And also you get access to a chat room where, again, we discuss the episodes, we give out book recommendations, all kinds of stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 此外，你还可以进入聊天室，在那里我们同样会讨论剧集、提供书单推荐，以及各种类似的事情。

sentences.en: And you can sign up for this, the Rest is History Club at restishistorypod.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 restishistorypod.com 注册加入《历史的余味》俱乐部。

sentences.en: That is restishistorypod.com.
sentences.zh: That is restishistorypod.com.

sentences.en: It's £6 a month and you become a friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 每月6英镑，你就能成为节目的挚友。

sentences.en: Now, just one tiny last bit of self-promotion for which I apologize.
sentences.zh: 现在，最后再做一点点自我推销，对此我表示抱歉。

sentences.en: We do also have a gold level member tier and they're called the Atholstans.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一个黄金会员等级，他们被称为“埃塞尔斯坦人”。

sentences.en: And they get all the friend of the show benefits.
sentences.zh: 他们可以获得所有挚友福利。

sentences.en: And if you join that, you get an invitation to two genuine, actual, real parties, Atholstans parties every year.
sentences.zh: 如果你加入那个等级，每年还会收到两次真正的、实体的、现实中的派对邀请，也就是“埃塞尔斯坦人派对”。

sentences.en: Dominic actually comes out of his hobbit hole.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克真的会从他的霍比特洞里走出来。

sentences.en: Amazing sight.
sentences.zh: 那场面真是太壮观了。

sentences.en: I mean, am I not going to just address the party on Zoom?
sentences.zh: 我是说，难道我就不能在Zoom上向派对致辞吗？

sentences.en: I fear I'm not.
sentences.zh: 恐怕不行。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we have the first date, which I think is Saturday, the 21st of May.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，我们有了第一个日期，我想是5月21日，星期六。

sentences.en: And of course, I'm tremendously excited about it.
sentences.zh: 当然，我对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's in central London.
sentences.zh: 地点在伦敦市中心。

sentences.en: It's in a pub.
sentences.zh: 在一家酒吧里。

sentences.en: So that's very convenient for me, less convenient for you.
sentences.zh: 这对我很方便，对你来说就不那么方便了。

sentences.en: My argument to have it at Banbury Station, sadly, was vetoed.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我提议在班伯里车站举办的建议被否决了。

sentences.en: But the whole Rest is History team will be there.
sentences.zh: 但整个《历史的余味》团队都会到场。

sentences.en: Everybody will be there.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会去。

sentences.en: All the lads.
sentences.zh: 所有的伙计们。

sentences.en: And we're going to be doing a pub quiz for the Atholstans as well online.
sentences.zh: 我们还要为“埃塞尔斯坦人”在线举办一场酒吧问答游戏。

sentences.en: And that is coming out this weekend on the Sunday, the 13th and Monday, the 14th of March.
sentences.zh: 活动将在本周末，即3月13日周日和14日周一推出。

sentences.en: So we've got to get the questions together, all kinds of stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得把问题准备好，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: We do indeed.
sentences.zh: 我们确实得这么做。

sentences.en: We do indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So that's restishistorypod.com if you want to join the club and you get all these tremendous benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想加入俱乐部并获得所有这些巨大的福利，请访问 restishistorypod.com。

sentences.en: And of course, crucially, you will get early access to the remainder of the episodes on this story.
sentences.zh: 当然，最关键的是，你可以提前收听这个故事的后续剧集。

sentences.en: The fall of the USSR, the creation of Russia, the Russian Federation in the 1990s, and the rise of Putin.
sentences.zh: 苏联的解体、俄罗斯的建立、九十年代的俄罗斯联邦以及普京的崛起。

sentences.en: And of course, if you don't want to join all that and you are absolutely bridling and furious at having the stories been interrupted by this shameless self-promotion,
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你不想加入这一切，并且因为这些无耻的自我推销打断了故事而感到愤怒和恼火，

sentences.en: don't worry, you can carry on listening for free and we will get right back to it right now.
sentences.zh: 别担心，你可以继续免费收听，我们现在就回到正题。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is enough shameless self-promotion.
sentences.zh: 是的，无耻的自我推销到此为止。

sentences.en: Right, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 好了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: So you were just saying before the break that a lot of the people at the top of the Soviet Union are not burning with kind of revolutionary communist zeal.
sentences.zh: 你刚才在休息前说，苏联高层的许多人并没有那种革命共产主义的狂热。

sentences.en: And the question I asked you was on Andropov.
sentences.zh: 我问你的问题是关于安德罗波夫的。

sentences.en: He's the guy who notoriously has the cold.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个出了名患有感冒的人。

sentences.en: It lasts for what, kind of four years, three years or something?
sentences.zh: 那场感冒持续了大概四年、三年还是多久？

sentences.en: I mean, basically, he's incapacitated for the whole period of his term of general secretary.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上在他担任总书记的整个任期内，他都丧失了工作能力。

sentences.en: And then he succeeded by Chinenko, who is kind of, in many ways, even more moribund.
sentences.zh: 随后继任他的是契尔年科，他在很多方面甚至更加垂死。

sentences.en: Are these guys people who, you know, so Andropov is a very smart guy.
sentences.zh: 这些人是……你知道，安德罗波夫是个非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: He recognizes the Soviet Union has huge probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他意识到苏联存在巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Is he a believer, though?
sentences.zh: 但他是一个信徒吗？

sentences.en: He doesn't question the system.
sentences.zh: 他并不质疑这个体制。

sentences.en: He just thinks that the system needs a bit of tinkering.
sentences.zh: 他只是认为这个体制需要一点修补。

sentences.en: You know, apply the spanner here, a bit of oil there, and it will tick along fine.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里拧个扳手，那里加点油，它就能正常运转了。

sentences.en: He doesn't question the mission, I suppose, is what I would say.
sentences.zh: 我想我会说，他并不质疑这个使命。

sentences.en: So, I mean, Chinenko, he's a hack.
sentences.zh: 那么，契尔年科，他就是个平庸之辈。

sentences.en: He's just a party hack.
sentences.zh: 他只是个党棍。

sentences.en: Andropov is clever.
sentences.zh: 安德罗波夫很聪明。

sentences.en: He was the Soviet ambassador, I think, in Hungary during the Budapest uprising.
sentences.zh: 我想他在布达佩斯起义期间担任过苏联驻匈牙利大使。

sentences.en: So, he has taken from that a belief that you have to be strong.
sentences.zh: 所以，他从中得出的信念是必须保持强硬。

sentences.en: You know, you have to suppress dissent.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你必须镇压异见。

sentences.en: You can't let things.
sentences.zh: 你不能让事情……

sentences.en: But he also has taken a belief that you have to get in ahead.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也得出了一个信念，那就是必须防患于未然。

sentences.en: So, you know, you can't let yourself get in a situation where thousands of people are in the streets.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你不能让自己陷入成千上万人在街头抗议的境地。

sentences.en: You have to keep changing the system to make it work.
sentences.zh: 你必须不断改变体制以使其运作。

sentences.en: So, I don't think Andropov is in it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不认为安德罗波夫是那种人。

sentences.en: He's very severe.
sentences.zh: 他非常严厉。

sentences.en: He's very strict.
sentences.zh: 他非常严格。

sentences.en: He's very anti-corruption.
sentences.zh: 他非常反腐。

sentences.en: And he's clever.
sentences.zh: 而且他很聪明。

sentences.en: And he has read forbidden books.
sentences.zh: 他读过禁书。

sentences.en: And as Soviets, sort of the top brass are allowed to do, they're expected to do, to inform themselves.
sentences.zh: 作为苏联的高层，他们被允许，甚至被期望去阅读这些书，以充实自己。

sentences.en: And he's surrounded himself with aides who are relatively free thinking.
sentences.zh: 他身边围绕着一些思想相对自由的助手。

sentences.en: But he's still, I mean, everybody there believes that their model must triumph.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然……我的意思是，那里的每个人都相信他们的模式一定会胜利。

sentences.en: And they believe they're in a global competition with the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们相信自己正与美国进行全球竞争。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so, he is, you know, you said he was head of the KGB.
sentences.zh: 所以，你说过他是克格勃的首脑。

sentences.en: He's general secretary during the kind of the coldest days of the Cold War in the early 80s.
sentences.zh: 他在八十年代初冷战最寒冷的时期担任总书记。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, he is the guy who's in charge when Reagan is lambasting the Soviet Union as evil empire.
sentences.zh: 所以，当里根抨击苏联为“邪恶帝国”时，他就是那个掌权的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's 99 red balloons and two tribes.
sentences.zh: 当时还有《99个红气球》和《两个部落》这些歌。

sentences.en: Which is very frightening, by the way, for the Soviet leadership.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这对苏联领导层来说非常可怕。

sentences.en: They think the Americans are going to attack them.
sentences.zh: 他们认为美国人要攻击他们。

sentences.en: I mean, we did a podcast about this with Taylor Downing about nuclear war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们和泰勒·唐宁做过一期关于核战争的播客。

sentences.en: They absolutely are terrified that the Americans are going to attack them firSt.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对非常害怕美国人会先发制人攻击他们。

sentences.en: But, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的。

sentences.en: So, Andropov takes over.
sentences.zh: 所以，安德罗波夫接手了。

sentences.en: Brezhnev dies.
sentences.zh: 勃列日涅夫去世了。

sentences.en: I mean, Brezhnev basically died multiple times and was literally brought back from the dead.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，勃列日涅夫基本上死过好几次，又被硬生生地从死亡线上拉了回来。

sentences.en: You know, he's sort of resuscitated and dragged around as this sort of embalmed figure in the late 1970s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在七十年代末，他就像一个被防腐处理过的人偶一样被复苏并拖来拖去。

sentences.en: Andropov succeeds in November 82 and is there until February 84.
sentences.zh: 安德罗波夫在82年11月继位，一直到84年2月。

sentences.en: And as you said, he's basically ill the whole time.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他基本上整个任期都在生病。

sentences.en: I mean, they literally, you know, on one side of his bed, there'll be the man with the nuclear briefcase.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们真的……你知道，在他床的一边是拿着核手提箱的人。

sentences.en: And the other side of his bed will be the nurses keeping him alive.
sentences.zh: 而床的另一边是维持他生命的护士。

sentences.en: And then he dies.
sentences.zh: 然后他去世了。

sentences.en: Now, the person he wants to succeed him is the crucial figure in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，他想要继任的人是本期播客的关键人物。

sentences.en: And for Putin, a figure of utter ignominy and shame in Russian history.
sentences.zh: 对于普京来说，这是一个在俄罗斯历史上极度屈辱和羞耻的人物。

sentences.en: As indeed he is for a lot of Russians.
sentences.zh: 正如许多俄罗斯人所认为的那样。

sentences.en: And that man is Mikhail Gorbachev.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫。

sentences.en: That's the man that Andropov wants to take over.
sentences.zh: 那就是安德罗波夫想要接班的人。

sentences.en: But he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但他没能接班。

sentences.en: He's too young.
sentences.zh: 他太年轻了。

sentences.en: So the other people in the Politburo, they bypass him and they get this old hack, Chanenko, who is another sort of, I mean, he's dying when he takes over.
sentences.zh: 所以政治局里的其他人绕过了他，找来了那个老党棍契尔年科，他又是那种……我的意思是，他接手时就已经快死了。

sentences.en: And he's there from February 84 to the spring of 85.
sentences.zh: 他从84年2月一直待到85年春天。

sentences.en: So what was it about Gorbachev that Andropov had seen?
sentences.zh: 那么安德罗波夫在戈尔巴乔夫身上看到了什么呢？

sentences.en: That's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: So Gorbachev is a generation younger.
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫年轻一代。

sentences.en: He's the youngest guy, I think, pretty much on the Politburo.
sentences.zh: 我想他几乎是政治局里最年轻的人。

sentences.en: He joins in 1980 and he's 49, which is incredibly young by the standards of the Soviet leadership.
sentences.zh: 他在1980年加入时才49岁，按照苏联领导层的标准，这极其年轻。

sentences.en: And he has a glamorous wife.
sentences.zh: 而且他有一位迷人的妻子。

sentences.en: He does, right?
sentences.zh: 确实，对吧？

sentences.en: He's a very clever wife who's a very important, I mean, hugely important figure for him.
sentences.zh: 他有一位非常聪明的妻子，她非常重要，我的意思是，对他来说是一个极其重要的人物。

sentences.en: His chief advisor.
sentences.zh: 他的首席顾问。

sentences.en: I mean, his real soulmate.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他真正的灵魂伴侣。

sentences.en: So Gorbachev is from a place called Stavropol.
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫来自一个叫斯塔夫罗波尔的地方。

sentences.en: He's from a little village called, what's it called?
sentences.zh: 他来自一个小村庄，叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Privolnoir, I think it's called.
sentences.zh: 我想是叫普里沃利诺耶。

sentences.en: And he's from peasant stock.
sentences.zh: 他出身于农民家庭。

sentences.en: He's bright.
sentences.zh: 他很聪明。

sentences.en: He's super bright.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明。

sentences.en: He's gone to Moscow State University.
sentences.zh: 他考上了莫斯科国立大学。

sentences.en: And I think he's read law.
sentences.zh: 我想他学的是法律。

sentences.en: He's got a birthmark on his forehead.
sentences.zh: 他额头上有一块胎记。

sentences.en: He does indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He's traveled.
sentences.zh: 他去过很多地方。

sentences.en: So he's been abroad.
sentences.zh: 所以他去过国外。

sentences.en: He even went on a three-week driving holiday in France with Royce.
sentences.zh: 他甚至和赖莎在法国进行过为期三周的自驾游。

sentences.en: And they sort of drove around France and said, God, you know, this place is so much better than the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他们开车游览法国时说，天哪，你知道，这个地方比苏联好多了。

sentences.en: You know, this is the sort of classic thing that often happens when people are posted to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种人们被派往西方后经常发生的典型情况。

sentences.en: He actually, one of his chief aides, one of his chief advisors is a man called Alexander Yakovlev,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的一位主要助手，他的一位首席顾问，是一个叫亚历山大·雅科夫列夫的人，

sentences.en: who had been ambassador to Canada and basically had exactly the same kind of crisis of confidence.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任驻加拿大大使，基本上也经历了完全相同的信心危机。

sentences.en: You know, he got to Canada and was like, oh, my God, this place is great.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他到了加拿大后就觉得，天哪，这个地方太棒了。

sentences.en: But when Gorbachev becomes general secretary, he's still a believer.
sentences.zh: 但当戈尔巴乔夫成为总书记时，他仍然是一个信徒。

sentences.en: I mean, just because he's got a nice camembert in France, it doesn't mean that he thinks…
sentences.zh: 我是说，仅仅因为他在法国吃到了一块美味的卡门贝尔奶酪，并不意味着他认为……

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Absolutely, Tom.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Absolutely, he's a believer.
sentences.zh: 绝对，他是一个信徒。

sentences.en: He is idealistic.
sentences.zh: 他是个理想主义者。

sentences.en: And this is one of the great problems with Gorbachev.
sentences.zh: 而这就是戈尔巴乔夫面临的巨大问题之一。

sentences.en: Now, Gorbachev is a fascinating character because, of course, everybody listening to this, by and large, will think, oh, Gorby, a nice guy.
sentences.zh: 现在，戈尔巴乔夫是一个引人入胜的人物，因为当然，听这个节目的绝大多数人都会认为，哦，戈尔比，是个好人。

sentences.en: You know, Nobel Peace Prize winner.
sentences.zh: 你知道，诺贝尔和平奖得主。

sentences.en: Top man.
sentences.zh: 顶尖人物。

sentences.en: Of course, in Russia, he is regarded with absolute contempt.
sentences.zh: 当然，在俄罗斯，他被视为绝对的蔑视对象。

sentences.en: And I have to say, when you start to dig into the story and you think about Gorbachev in a slightly more detached way, I mean,
sentences.zh: 我必须说，当你开始深入挖掘这个故事，并以一种稍微超然的方式思考戈尔巴乔夫时，我是说，

sentences.en: we've done a lot of weak and failed leaders on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在本播客中讨论过很多软弱和失败的领导人。

sentences.en: And although it pains me to say it because he's an admirable man in so many ways.
sentences.zh: 虽然说出来让我很痛苦，因为他在很多方面都是一个令人钦佩的人。

sentences.en: I mean, but when he leaves office, he's only in there for six years.
sentences.zh: 我是说，但他离任时，他只在位了六年。

sentences.en: And when he leaves, his country has completely and utterly fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 而当他离开时，他的国家已经彻底分崩离析了。

sentences.en: Now, some people would say that's because the problems are too great.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人会说那是因为问题太大了。

sentences.en: But I think Gorbachev, I think almost all historians, actually, who really work on this, people like Robert Service or Vladislav Zubok,
sentences.zh: 但我认为戈尔巴乔夫，实际上几乎所有真正研究这一课题的历史学家，比如罗伯特·瑟维斯或弗拉迪斯拉夫·祖博克，

sentences.en: who wrote a brilliant book called Collapse that came out last year, The Fall of the Soviet Union, they would just say Gorbachev is a complete and utter disaster.
sentences.zh: 他们去年写了一本精彩的书叫《崩溃：苏联的解体》，他们只会说戈尔巴乔夫是一场彻头彻尾的灾难。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: He's idealistic, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他是个理想主义者，汤姆。

sentences.en: He's bright.
sentences.zh: 他很聪明。

sentences.en: He and Raisa have spent loads of time talking about the future of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他和赖莎花了很多时间讨论苏联的未来。

sentences.en: They like talking to other kind of intellectually kind of people.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢与那种知识分子类型的人交谈。

sentences.en: Gorbachev is also very canny.
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫也非常精明。

sentences.en: So he's been able to get up the kind of greasy pole.
sentences.zh: 所以他能够在那条充满竞争的仕途上步步高升。

sentences.en: These powerful patrons like Andropov think a lot of him.
sentences.zh: 像安德罗波夫这样有权势的赞助人非常看重他。

sentences.en: He says to Raisa when he joins the, I think it's when he joined the Politburo, he said, we can't live like this any longer.
sentences.zh: 当他加入，我想是加入政治局时，他对赖莎说，我们不能再这样生活下去了。

sentences.en: And he's determined to fix the system.
sentences.zh: 他决心修复这个体制。

sentences.en: But he goes about fixing it in such a politically incompetent.
sentences.zh: 但他修复它的方式在政治上是如此无能。

sentences.en: I mean, again, it slightly pains me to say it, but he fixes it in such an inept way that absolutely everything gets worse.
sentences.zh: 我是说，再说一次，说出来让我有点痛苦，但他修复它的方式如此笨拙，以至于一切都变得更糟了。

sentences.en: He does too much, too quickly, too many different areas, and everything falls apart.
sentences.zh: 他做得太多、太快，涉及的领域太多，结果一切都土崩瓦解了。

sentences.en: And you said, was he a believer?
sentences.zh: 你问，他是一个信徒吗？

sentences.en: He's absolutely a believer.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是一个信徒。

sentences.en: So Vladislav Zubok brings this out really well in his book.
sentences.zh: 弗拉迪斯拉夫·祖博克在他的书中很好地阐述了这一点。

sentences.en: He says, you know, Gorbachev is obsessed with Lenin.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，戈尔巴乔夫对列宁着了迷。

sentences.en: I mean, this is so much like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太像那样了。

sentences.en: You're parallel with your Christianity stuff about people who, you know, people who would kind of Oliver Cromwell or somebody reading the Bible to guide them.
sentences.zh: 你关于基督教的那些类比，比如奥利弗·克伦威尔或某人通过读圣经来指导自己。

sentences.en: Gorbachev has Lenin's sort of works on his desk, and he will sort of dip into them in the way that people sometimes dip into the Bible.
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫的桌上放着列宁的著作，他会像人们有时翻阅圣经那样去翻阅它们。

sentences.en: He will dip into them to try and get inspiration for what he needs to do.
sentences.zh: 他会翻阅它们，试图为自己需要做的事情寻找灵感。

sentences.en: And he becomes convinced, he is convinced that the Soviet Union has taken a wrong turn since the 1920s, and it needs to get back to Lenin's vision.
sentences.zh: 他变得深信不疑，他确信苏联自20世纪20年代以来走错了方向，需要回到列宁的愿景中去。

sentences.en: He idealizes Lenin, and he thinks Lenin had a vision that was a more democratic, free, open, creative.
sentences.zh: 他理想化了列宁，认为列宁的愿景更民主、更自由、更开放、更具创造性。

sentences.en: And if I can get back to that, we'll establish true communism, and then we'll turn this sort of sinking ship around, if you can turn a sinking ship around.
sentences.zh: 如果我能回到那个愿景，我们就能建立真正的共产主义，然后我们就能扭转这艘沉船，如果沉船还能扭转的话。

sentences.en: So that's quite a kind of abstract sense of mission.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种相当抽象的使命感。

sentences.en: But I – maybe I've got this wrong – but I thought that he was also focused on a very specific problem,
sentences.zh: 但我——也许我理解错了——但我以为他也专注于一个非常具体的问题，

sentences.en: which was that the Soviet economy was massively distorted by defense spending.
sentences.zh: 那就是苏联经济被国防开支严重扭曲了。

sentences.en: So they're spending, what, 20%, 25%?
sentences.zh: 所以他们花费了，多少，20%还是25%？

sentences.en: No, it's probably not – that's actually been exaggerated.
sentences.zh: 不，可能不是——那其实被夸大了。

sentences.en: It's about 15%, I think, is the latest estimate.
sentences.zh: 据最新估计，大约是15%。

sentences.en: But still, quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 但仍然相当多。

sentences.en: It is, but it's – If he's going to – if they're going to, you know, guns to butter.
sentences.zh: 确实，但如果他要——如果他们要，你知道，从大炮转向黄油。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Then they need to make things up with the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 那么他们就需要与西方和解。

sentences.en: So he does that very effectively.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常有效地做到了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very good at that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他在这方面非常擅长。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He definitely kind of removes the chill from the Cold War very effectively, which is why people in the West rate him so highly.
sentences.zh: 他确实非常有效地消除了冷战的寒意，这就是为什么西方人对他评价如此之高。

sentences.en: But as someone who is ideologically committed to Marxist-Leninism, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但作为一个在意识形态上忠于马克思列宁主义的人，我是说，

sentences.en: isn't it a definition of the job that kind of trying to construct an economy that will provide Soviet citizens with all the kind of consumer durables and gizmos that you get in the West is bound to fail?
sentences.zh: 试图构建一个能为苏联公民提供西方那种消费耐用品和小玩意的经济体，这难道不是注定要失败的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, there's just no way it can be done.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这根本是不可能做到的。

sentences.en: No, I don't agree with that.
sentences.zh: 不，我不同意这一点。

sentences.en: I actually don't agree with either of those things.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这两点我都不赞同。

sentences.en: So first of all, the defense spending, that has become a very comforting myth that the West tells itself about the Soviet Union, particularly in America,
sentences.zh: 首先，国防开支，这已经成为西方关于苏联，特别是在美国，对自己讲述的一个非常令人宽慰的神话，

sentences.en: that we crippled – we won the Cold War by increasing defense spending so much that they couldn't keep up.
sentences.zh: 即我们通过增加国防开支，让他们无法跟上，从而赢得了冷战。

sentences.en: But most historians, I think, would now say they could keep up.
sentences.zh: 但我想大多数历史学家现在会说，他们是能够跟上的。

sentences.en: I mean, they have – With defense spending.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们有——在国防开支方面。

sentences.en: Yeah, they've done it since the 40s.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们从40年代起就一直在这样做。

sentences.en: They could have carried on doing it.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以继续这样做。

sentences.en: I mean, that defense spending is not what brings the Soviet Union down.
sentences.zh: 我是说，国防开支并不是导致苏联垮台的原因。

sentences.en: Second point – I've forgotten what your second point was, Tom.
sentences.zh: 第二点——我忘了你的第二点是什么了，汤姆。

sentences.en: Oh, consumer durables.
sentences.zh: 哦，消费耐用品。

sentences.en: Well, there is a very good example of a communist country that has embraced a consumer economy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一个非常好的共产主义国家拥抱消费经济的例子。

sentences.en: That's China.
sentences.zh: 那就是中国。

sentences.en: And the Chinese – I mean, Deng Xiaoping supposedly said something to the effect that somebody – his son asked him what he thought of Gorbachev, and he said,
sentences.zh: 而且中国人——我是说邓小平据说说过类似的话，有人——他的儿子问他对戈尔巴乔夫的看法，他说，

sentences.en: I think Gorbachev's a complete idiot.
sentences.zh: 我认为戈尔巴乔夫是个彻头彻尾的白痴。

sentences.en: Yes, but this is communism with Chinese characteristics, which basically means a kind of freedom to ignore aspects of communism that don't gel with making money.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这是具有中国特色的社会主义，这基本上意味着可以自由地忽略那些与赚钱不符的共产主义方面。

sentences.en: But Leninism absolutely – I mean, Leninism is all about kind of collectivization.
sentences.zh: 但列宁主义绝对——我是说列宁主义的核心就是集体化。

sentences.en: It's all about suppression of private enterprise.
sentences.zh: 它完全是关于压制私营企业的。

sentences.en: But I think most historians would say, well, first of all, that's not what Gorbachev himself thinks.
sentences.zh: 但我认为大多数历史学家会说，首先，这并不是戈尔巴乔夫本人的想法。

sentences.en: He thinks Lenin's new economic policy in the 1920s after the Russian Civil War did allow some space for limited private enterprise and that they can move towards a mixed economy.
sentences.zh: 他认为列宁在俄国内战后20年代的新经济政策确实为有限的私营企业留出了一些空间，他们可以转向混合经济。

sentences.en: I think one of the big problems with the Soviet Union is it's become so reliant on imports paid for with oil revenue,
sentences.zh: 我认为苏联的一个大问题是它变得太依赖石油收入支付的进口，

sentences.en: and it's completely failed to develop its own kind of consumer industries.
sentences.zh: 而且它完全未能发展自己的消费产业。

sentences.en: So it's like Saudi Arabia with snow a bit.
sentences.zh: 所以它有点像带雪的沙特阿拉伯。

sentences.en: Is that what the – what do they do?
sentences.zh: 那是——他们做什么？

sentences.en: Do they spend their raw money on snow?
sentences.zh: 他们把赚来的钱花在雪上吗？

sentences.en: No, but I mean, it's the – you know, notoriously, economies that have lots of oil tend to be dysfunctional.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，众所周知，拥有大量石油的经济体往往功能失调。

sentences.en: Well, yes, Iran is a good example from the 70s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，伊朗是70年代的一个好例子。

sentences.en: We talked about Iran a lot in previous podcasts.
sentences.zh: 我们在之前的播客中谈论了很多关于伊朗的话题。

sentences.en: And I think, yes, it's incredibly dysfunctional.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的，它功能极其失调。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an unbelievably complicated economy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个令人难以置信的复杂经济体。

sentences.en: No one – I mean, when Gorbachev is given – they're talking about this thing called the law of state enterprise,
sentences.zh: 没有人——我是说，当戈尔巴乔夫被给予——他们谈论的是这个叫《国营企业法》的东西，

sentences.en: which is going to be this law that's going to allow a little bit of more freedom for factories to keep their money and to invest it and that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 这将是一项允许工厂保留更多资金并进行投资等方面的法律。

sentences.en: Gorbachev says at one point, you know, I basically don't understand this.
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫有一次说，你知道，我基本上不明白这个。

sentences.en: And nobody really understands that.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人真正明白这一点。

sentences.en: Well, I feel sympathy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我表示同情。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, he's trying to mend a machine for which there is no instruction manual.
sentences.zh: 我是说，基本上，他是在试图修理一台没有说明书的机器。

sentences.en: I think there's a degree of that.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一定程度的这种原因。

sentences.en: But I think he's also – you see, the thing is he's trying to mend this machine, which has incredibly complicated kind of supply chain networks,
sentences.zh: 但我认为他也是——你看，问题在于他试图修理这台机器，它有极其复杂的供应链网络，

sentences.en: and it has this weird cashless system that enterprises use with each other, whereas citizens use cash and you can't change one to the other.
sentences.zh: 而且它有一种奇怪的无现金系统，企业之间使用，而公民使用现金，两者无法互换。

sentences.en: I mean, it's completely mad, but that's the way – it's a bit like any massive sclerotic institution.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这完全是疯了，但这就是方式——这有点像任何庞大而僵化的机构。

sentences.en: Once you start to fiddle with it, it becomes very difficult to stop it from falling apart.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始摆弄它，就很难阻止它分崩离析。

sentences.en: But the other thing is he combines this with – so he has the perestroika, which is restructuring, which kind of has political and economic developments,
sentences.zh: 但另一件事是他将此与——所以他有“改革”（Perestroika），即重组，这在政治和经济上都有发展，

sentences.en: but he combines it with glasnost, which is openness.
sentences.zh: 但他将其与“公开性”（Glasnost）结合起来，即开放。

sentences.en: And that's in the wake of Chernobyl.
sentences.zh: 那是在切尔诺贝利事件之后。

sentences.en: So Chernobyl – the explosion at Chernobyl is in April 1986.
sentences.zh: 所以切尔诺贝利——切尔诺贝利的爆炸发生在1986年4月。

sentences.en: And after that, Gorbachev thinks, well, I need to increase the speed.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，戈尔巴乔夫想，嗯，我需要加快速度。

sentences.en: We need to have more newspapers.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多的报纸。

sentences.en: We need to have more discussion.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多的讨论。

sentences.en: And why does Chernobyl have that effect on him?
sentences.zh: 为什么切尔诺贝利对他有那样的影响？

sentences.en: Because I think he's shocked by the incompetence, by the cover-ups, by the ineptitude of the managers, by the way the atomic industry has been run,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为他被管理者的无能、掩盖真相、笨拙，以及原子工业的运作方式所震惊，

sentences.en: by their lies, all of that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 被他们的谎言，所有这些事情所震惊。

sentences.en: You know, Gorbachev, of course, he's complicit in covering it up a bit because he's the general secretary and he kind of feels like he has to.
sentences.zh: 你知道，戈尔巴乔夫当然也参与了掩盖真相，因为他是总书记，他觉得他必须这样做。

sentences.en: But he still thinks, okay, we need to – you know, we just need to be more open and we need to be more creative.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然认为，好吧，我们需要——你知道，我们只需要更开放，我们需要更有创造力。

sentences.en: Crucially, one of the things he does now, one of the things we haven't talked about at all, which is very important for understanding Putin, is the Soviet Union –
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，他现在做的一件事，我们完全没有谈论过的一件事，这对理解普京非常重要，那就是苏联——

sentences.en: and I know we have a lot of very kind of – to us, young listeners – the Soviet Union is not anything like a nation state.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们有很多非常——对我们来说，年轻的听众——苏联根本不像一个民族国家。

sentences.en: And it doesn't even really see itself as an empire.
sentences.zh: 它甚至不把自己看作一个帝国。

sentences.en: So it's got 15 republics going all the way from Estonia – I mean, it's a mad state in many ways.
sentences.zh: 所以它有15个加盟共和国，一直延伸到爱沙尼亚——我是说，它在很多方面是一个疯狂的国家。

sentences.en: It's existed, you know, one or another since the 20s.
sentences.zh: 它存在了，你知道，从20年代起就以某种形式存在。

sentences.en: But it's got – going all the way from Estonia to kind of Tajikistan.
sentences.zh: 但它有——从爱沙尼亚一直延伸到塔吉克斯坦。

sentences.en: And the Russians are about – roughly about 50% of that, you know, the Russian population.
sentences.zh: 而俄罗斯人大约占——大约50%，你知道，俄罗斯人口。

sentences.en: And there has always been the issue of nationalism.
sentences.zh: 而且一直存在民族主义的问题。

sentences.en: You know, there's always been tensions in the Caucasus, in Central Asia, in the Baltics and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，高加索、中亚、波罗的海等地一直存在紧张局势。

sentences.en: And Gorbachev has this idea that by basically devolving a lot of power to the republics – I mean, devolution, Tom, what could possibly go wrong –
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫有一个想法，通过基本上将大量权力下放给各共和国——我是说，权力下放，汤姆，这能出什么错——

sentences.en: devolving power to the republics, that will invigorate the system.
sentences.zh: 将权力下放给各共和国，那将激活这个体制。

sentences.en: You know, but at the same time, he wants to open everything up so people can debate things more freely.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但与此同时，他想开放一切，让人们更自由地辩论。

sentences.en: So that will obviously give nationalism more room to sort of flourish.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然会给民族主义更多的空间来蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: But he also combines that with an attack on what he sees as the corruption of the old elites.
sentences.zh: 但他还将其与对他所认为的旧精英腐败的攻击结合起来。

sentences.en: So the old elites are embattled.
sentences.zh: 所以旧精英们陷入了困境。

sentences.en: People are talking about new ideas.
sentences.zh: 人们在谈论新思想。

sentences.en: But they're also being given more power.
sentences.zh: 但他们也被赋予了更多的权力。

sentences.en: The whole thing – it's a sort of – he creates unwittingly a kind of breeding ground for all these kind of nationalistic movements to thrive.
sentences.zh: 整个事情——这是一种——他在无意中为所有这些民族主义运动的繁荣创造了温床。

sentences.en: And you see it as early as 1986.
sentences.zh: 早在1986年，你就能看到这种苗头了。

sentences.en: You see it in Kazakhstan and in the Baltics and Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 在哈萨克斯坦、波罗的海地区和乌克兰，你都能看到。

sentences.en: Movement's calling for new language rights and, you know, opposing power stations and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 运动呼吁新的语言权利，你知道的，反对发电站建设等等诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So the seeds of trouble are there even after he's only been there a year.
sentences.zh: 所以，即便他上任才一年，动荡的种子就已经埋下了。

sentences.en: And Dominic, do we know what Putin is doing?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们知道普京在做什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes, we do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们知道。

sentences.en: So this is in St. Petersburg still, is he?
sentences.zh: 所以他当时还在圣彼得堡，对吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: This is the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 这正是耐人寻味的地方。

sentences.en: He's not.
sentences.zh: 他不在那里。

sentences.en: So around about the point where Chernenko gave way to Gorbachev, where Gorbachev came into power,
sentences.zh: 大约在契尔年科让位给戈尔巴乔夫，戈尔巴乔夫上台的时候，

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin has been working for the KGB since the late 70s.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京自70年代末以来就一直在克格勃工作。

sentences.en: And he has now been posted to Dresden, East Germany.
sentences.zh: 他现在已经被派往东德的德累斯顿。

sentences.en: Of course he has.
sentences.zh: 他当然被派去了。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So what he's doing – and he's doing sort of slightly – it seems – there are different stories.
sentences.zh: 那么他在做什么呢——他做的事情有点——看起来——有不同的说法。

sentences.en: Some people say he's just compiling information about dissidents.
sentences.zh: 有人说他只是在搜集异见人士的信息。

sentences.en: Some people say actually he's trying to sort of forge links with the sort of remnants of the Red Army faction, the Baader-Meinhof gang in West Germany.
sentences.zh: 也有人说他实际上是在试图与西德的“红军派”残余势力，也就是巴德-迈因霍夫集团建立联系。

sentences.en: We don't know because, of course, it's secret.
sentences.zh: 我们不得而知，因为这当然是机密。

sentences.en: But what we know is he's watching all this from outside.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道的是，他正在局外观察这一切。

sentences.en: So he has left a state that he thinks is powerful, you know, strong, respected in the world, high status.
sentences.zh: 他离开了一个他认为强大、稳固、在世界上受人尊敬、地位崇高的国家。

sentences.en: And he sees this guy trying to reform it, to change things.
sentences.zh: 然后他看到这个人试图改革它，试图改变现状。

sentences.en: And that's really important, I think, that Putin is watching it from outside.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点非常重要，普京是在局外观察这一切的。

sentences.en: And he's watching it, frankly, with horror.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，他是怀着恐惧在观察这一切。

sentences.en: And he's in East Germany, which has a higher standard of living relative to the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 而且他身处东德，那里的生活水平相对苏联来说更高。

sentences.en: It does indeed, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，没错。

sentences.en: So he is alert to, presumably, some of the problems that the Soviet economy faces.
sentences.zh: 所以他大概对苏联经济面临的一些问题很敏感。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't think – you asked if Putin was a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 我不认为——你问过普京是否是共产主义者。

sentences.en: He's certainly not a communist now and has not been since the fall of the USSR.
sentences.zh: 他现在肯定不是共产主义者，自苏联解体以来就不是了。

sentences.en: But what he is, is a believer in the Russian world, in the Russian sphere of influence.
sentences.zh: 但他是一个“俄罗斯世界”的信徒，坚信俄罗斯的势力范围。

sentences.en: And I think that's what's going to trouble him as we get into the late 80s and early 90s, that that starts to fragment and fall apart.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是随着我们进入80年代末和90年代初，让他感到不安的原因，因为这一切开始分崩离析。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's enough for today.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想今天就到这里吧。

sentences.en: So that's the end of today's episode.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天节目的结尾。

sentences.zh: 请明天继续收听，了解80年代末戈尔巴乔夫的情况如何开始真正崩溃，以及最终苏联本身的命运。

sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史余音》（The Rest is History）。
